subject: Acme: feature parity & perf test next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: None
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo  recap & next steps

Hi Lena  great call today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goals you called out: validate feature parity with your current hyperscaler API (function/tool calling, structured JSON outputs, streaming), measure latency/throughput, and estimate per-token cost at scale.
- Risk/constraints: must run at least one test against a private VPC dataset (PII scrubbed) and include a procurement timeline for committed capacity if results look good.

Proposed next steps: 
1) Redwood will run three comparative tests (see attachments):
   - Streaming function-calls parity test (latency, order, streaming reliability)
   - Structured output / schema conformance test (precision + hallucination checks)
   - Throughput & cost sweep (various batch sizes + KV cache warm/cold)
2) We'll coordinate with your dev team for a shared sample set (10k queries) and a short script to replay requests.
3) We aim to deliver a short technical report and perf dashboard within 7 business days after we receive the sample set.

I've attached a short test-plan PDF and a demo recording with the streaming sample. Looping in our SE, Dylan, to propose the concrete test matrix.

Thanks 
Marissa 
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Hi Marissa  thanks for the clear recap. This looks good. A couple of clarifying items from our side before you run anything: 

- For the streaming function-calls parity test: can you include checks for function call reliability when the model needs to call an external tool mid-stream (we've seen some hyperscalers reset streams in those cases)?
- For structured outputs: please add a schema conformance score and an example of how you'd enforce deterministic keys in the JSON outputs.
- On procurement: if results are positive, procurement will need an estimated committed monthly spend and the SLO/latency guarantees for a Dedicated pool.

We'll prepare a scrubbed sample dataset (PII removed) and aim to send it by Monday. CCing procurement so they have visibility.

Lena Ortiz

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo  recap & next steps

Thanks, Lena  looping in Dylan (SE) and Aditya (Sales Eng) to confirm the test matrix and add the enforcement checks for structured outputs. High-level answers up front: 

- Streaming function-calls: we'll exercise 3 scenarios: (A) simple function call mid-stream, (B) nested function calls (tool calls that trigger another call), (C) function call with heavy streaming payloads (stream resumes). We'll capture fail/retry counts, stream reset events, and wall-clock latency per token.
- Structured outputs: we will run schema conformance tests using JSON Schema validation and provide a conformance score (pass rate + field-level precision). We'll include deterministic key ordering as part of our post-processing comparator.
- Dedicated pricing: will share a committed capacity line item and latency SLOs in the procurement-ready doc.

Dylan  can you confirm the matrix below and attach the replay script we plan to use? Also please include an estimate for how long the runs will take on a 4xA10 Dedicated pool (so procurement has cycle time numbers).

Proposed matrix (high level):
- Streaming function-calls: 1k requests per scenario, record stream stability + function output correctness.
- Structured outputs: 2k requests with 5 JSON schemas, check conformance + hallucination samples (100 manual checks).
- Throughput/cost sweep: batch sizes [1,4,8,16], KV cache warm vs cold, measure tokens/sec and $/1M tokens.

Thanks 
Marissa

Attachments: acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (stub)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Oct 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme test matrix + replay script

Hi all  thanks for the details. Attached is the replay script (bash + Python harness) and a slightly more detailed test-plan excerpt. Key technical notes: 

- Streaming function-calls: our harness uses a streaming websocket client that simulates network jitter and partial chunk delivery; we assert at each stream chunk boundary whether the function-call token sequence is intact. We'll log any stream resets and the last successful function output.
- Tool/function calling: to simulate external tool latency, we inject configurable delays (50ms, 200ms, 1s) and verify the model defers/awaits tool responses without dropping the stream.
- Structured outputs: we'll run JSON Schema checks and an automated hallucination detector (fuzzy match against expected values). Output examples will be scored and we will provide a field-level precision/recall table in the report.
- Metrics & infra: for a 4xA10 Dedicated pool we estimate: full matrix run (approx 6k total requests) ~ 2 hours wall time; ephemeral infra cost estimate: ~$120 for the run (compute only, does not include storage/engineering time).

Next steps: 
1) Lena  share the scrubbed sample set and the 5 JSON schemas as a single zipped archive (we'll validate before running).
2) Procurement  if you want a committed pricing quote, we'll include a Dedicated commit SKU and the SLOs in the MPA.

Attaching: redwood-acme-test-plan-v1.pdf (detailed excerpt), replay-harness.tar.gz (script bundle).

Thanks 
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan@redwood.com
